key_insight: Lyris proposes combining layout guidance with persistent 3D memory to generate long, camera-controlled video walkthroughs from as little as one photo. The goal is to control where scene elements appear while keeping previously visited places consistent.
problem_solved: Long video generation must invent unseen areas without losing spatial control or changing familiar views when the camera returns. Memory alone lacks an anchor for unexplored regions, while text prompts cannot precisely position objects.
method: Use layout guidance as a spatial anchor for scene composition beyond the initial view.
Maintain persistent 3D memory to support consistency when revisiting generated areas.
Combine these signals for long, camera-controlled scene exploration; implementation details are not available in the truncated abstract.
impact: This approach could make generative walkthroughs more controllable and spatially coherent, benefiting virtual environment creation and scene exploration. The supplied excerpt does not report quantitative results.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input photo + layout guidance + 3D memory → long video walkthrough.
Top-down scene layout with object positions and a planned camera path.
Return-visit frame pair illustrating the goal of preserving scene consistency.
Exploration map distinguishing remembered regions from newly generated areas.
paper_title: Lyris: Layout-Guided Long Video Generation with Persistent 3D Memory
paper_authors: Chen Wang, Jiahui Huang, Riccardo de Lutio, Alex Trevithick, Bryan Chu
